address: Church Street, Otterbrook, near Tiverford, Devon EX16 9RW
entry: Wear something bright if you can. Ruth never liked black.

items.title: Music on entering
items.note: Nimrod, from Elgar’s Enigma Variations, played by Martin Bale.

items.title: Welcome
items.note: The Revd Philippa Gale, Rector of Otterbrook.

items.title: Hymn: The Lord’s my shepherd
items.note: Sung to Crimond. The words are on the sheet you are given at the door.

items.title: Reading: Ecclesiastes 3, verses 1 to 8
items.note: “To every thing there is a season.” Read by Ana Ellacott, Ruth’s granddaughter.

items.title: A life remembered
items.note: Tom Ellacott, Ruth’s son, with words from some of the children she taught.

items.title: Poem: Crossing the Bar
items.note: By Alfred, Lord Tennyson. Read by Jean Pascoe, who swam in the sea with Ruth every Sunday morning for forty years.

items.title: Music on leaving
items.note: Sheep may safely graze, by Bach. The retiring collection is for the Otterbrook School library, which Ruth started.

items.title: Tea in the village hall
items.note: Everyone is welcome. Her friends from the garden club are baking saffron buns to Ruth’s recipe.

items.title: A drink at the Otter Inn
items.note: For anyone not ready to go home.

items.title: A walk to Ruth’s bench above the river
items.note: About an hour there and back on a field path. Boots, and dogs on leads, are welcome.

people.name: The Otterbrook Singers
people.note: Ruth sang alto with them for thirty-one years.
